2: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of Asaph. I cried out to God; I cried aloud to God to hear me.
3: In the day of trouble I sought the Lord; through the night my outstretched hands did not grow weary; my soul refused to be comforted.
4: I remembered You, O God, and I groaned; I mused and my spirit grew faint. Selah
5: You have kept my eyes from closing; I am too troubled to speak.
6: I considered the days of old, the years long in the past.
7: At night I remembered my song; in my heart I mused, and my spirit pondered:
8: “Will the Lord spurn us forever and never show His favor again?
9: Is His loving devotion gone forever? Has His promise failed for all time?
10: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has His anger shut off His compassion?” Selah
11: So I said, “I am grieved that the right hand of the Most High has changed.”
12: I will remember the works of the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders of old.
13: I will reflect on all You have done and ponder Your mighty deeds.
14: Your way, O God, is holy. What god is so great as our God?
15: You are the God who works wonders; You display Your strength among the peoples.
16: With power You redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
17: The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and swirled; even the depths were shaken.
18: The clouds poured down water; the skies resounded with thunder; Your arrows flashed back and forth.
19: Your thunder resounded in the whirlwind; the lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and quaked.
20: Your path led through the sea, Your way through the mighty waters, but Your footprints were not to be found.
21: You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
